finding.claim: LinkSanitizer (HTML4, HTML5, and the Rails::HTML::LinkSanitizer alias) passes <script> elements and on* event-handler attributes through unchanged; its scrubber removes only <a> tags and href attributes.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled HTML passed to LinkSanitizer#sanitize, e.g. '' or ''.
finding.sink: Sanitizer output that a consumer renders as raw HTML (html_safe or raw), producing stored or reflected XSS.

trace.note: For elements, keep_node?(node) decides whether the node is removed
TargetScrubber#allowed_node? returns !super; 'script' and 'img' return true (kept), only 'a' is removed
scrub_attributes runs for every kept element
Attribute loop; onerror/onclick are not in @attributes
TargetScrubber#scrub_attribute? returns !super, which is @attributes.include?(name); only 'href' is removed, onerror is kept
Kept attributes go to scrub_attribute, which checks only URI, SVG ref, empty src and escaping; it never removes event handlers
properly_encode calls fragment.to_html, which emits <script> content raw and keeps on* attributes

finding.guards_checked: (1) Link allowlist is a removal list of 'a'/'href' only (sanitizer.rb:72-73). (2) CDATA escape (scrubbers.rb:67-71) does not affect script or on*. (3) Namespace prune (scrubbers.rb:106) applies only to namespaced nodes, not HTML <script>. (4) URI, SVG href and src checks (scrubbers.rb:169-181) inspect URI attributes only. (5) Only <a> is stripped. No control removes script elements or event-handler attributes. Severity depends on consumer: a bug if output is rendered as HTML; a trap for anyone who treats it as a sanitizer even if intended only as a link stripper. Verified by reading only, not executed.

finding.claim: SafeListSanitizer stores per-call tags and attributes in one shared @permit_scrubber per instance, so concurrent sanitize calls on the same instance can apply another call's allowlist.
finding.source: Per-call options[:tags] / options[:attributes] set by the application on one shared SafeListSanitizer instance used by multiple Ruby threads.
finding.sink: fragment.scrub!(@permit_scrubber) applies a looser or differently scoped allowlist to a request that should have a stricter one, letting disallowed tags or attributes survive.

trace.note: SafeList#initialize creates one @permit_scrubber per sanitizer instance
scrub: the elsif is always truthy because class defaults are set
Thread A writes @permit_scrubber.attributes; thread B can interleave here or before scrub!
scrub! reads whatever lists are current; Ruby may switch threads during the Nokogiri/Loofah callback, so the scrubber can use another request's list

finding.guards_checked: Per-call state is rewritten on every call with no per-call isolation or mutex. The scrubber option (sanitizer.rb:161) bypasses this path but is developer-supplied. tags=/attributes= dup and validate inputs (scrubbers.rb:58-64), which does not prevent the race. Low confidence: the Rails sanitize helper appears to create a new sanitizer per call (not verified here), so this matters only if an application shares a SafeListSanitizer instance across threads with differing per-call options.
